entries.root_cause: The initial governance branch inherited an unrelated runnable-application commit, so a documentation PR exposed API-role provisioning code that was outside its declared scope and carried an unreviewed least-privilege defect. Reconstructing the branch from the exact canonical base removed that runtime surface rather than misrepresenting it as fixed by documentation work.
horizontal_audit: declared PR scope versus actual diff

entries.root_cause: The initial governance branch inherited unrelated developer-runtime tooling, allowing a broken Makefile startup path to appear in a PR whose declared authority was documentation decisions. The branch was rebuilt from canonical main so developer tooling is no longer part of this proposal and must be handled only by a separately scoped implementation change.
horizontal_audit: declared PR scope versus actual diff

entries.root_cause: The initial governance branch inherited a file under the accepted Wave 2 protected substrate, violating both the stated docs-only purpose and the repository's immutable accepted-baseline contract. Exact-base branch reconstruction removed the undeclared protected-path mutation before acceptance.
horizontal_audit: declared PR scope versus actual diff

entries.root_cause: The initial governance branch inherited unrelated metric-history runtime code, causing a real per-request exhaustion defect to be reviewed inside a decision-record PR. Because that runtime was not authorized by this PR, the correct remediation was to remove the inherited code from the branch and leave any metric-history correction to its owning separately scoped authority.
horizontal_audit: declared PR scope versus actual diff

entries.root_cause: The initial governance branch inherited database bootstrap code with a hard-coded database-name defect even though the PR claimed decision-document scope. Rebuilding the branch from canonical main removed the bootstrap surface; configurable-database provisioning remains an implementation concern requiring its own scoped review rather than authority laundering through governance documentation.
horizontal_audit: declared PR scope versus actual diff

entries.root_cause: The first remediation credited a G1 implementation-scope falsifier as if it permanently guarded governance-only pull requests, but that probe exercised a G1-specific manifest and path policy and could not reject future docs/governance branch contamination. The repository now has a dedicated branch-classified governance scope validator, wired into deterministic assurance, plus a falsifier covering the exact runtime/substrate paths seen in the superseded PR.

The proposed response-orchestration record treated use of the existing G10 boundary as sufficient for automatic Alert-to-Incident creation even though accepted G10 explicitly excludes that authority. The proposal now requires a separately accepted bounded G10 extension before open_incident can cause any runtime effect and makes that dependency part of ordering and closure evidence.
